sourcedFrom: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B (cached from a 2023 capture; the document is undated on its face)
cleanIntro: A striker-fired, Glock-pattern 9mm with no manual safety, and Anderson's own book is unusually specific about two things. ⛔ THE SLIDE COMES BACK ONLY ABOUT 1/8 INCH (3 mm) to take it off, and going further resets the trigger so you have to start again. ⛔ AND NOTHING WET GOES NEAR THE FIRING PIN CHANNEL — Anderson says it twice, once as a cleaning notice and once as a lubrication rule, and tells you to hold the slide muzzle-DOWN while you work on the breech face so nothing runs into it.

steps.title: Magazine out first — there is no manual safety here
steps.action: Point the pistol somewhere safe, keep your finger outside the trigger guard, press the magazine catch and let the magazine come out.
steps.prose: ⛔ Anderson states the design fact plainly: this series has no manual safety, so the only thing standing between the trigger and a discharge is an empty chamber. Magazine first, always.
steps.aside: The Anderson Kiger series is designed without a manual safety. Consider it loaded and ready to fire until you have removed the magazine and confirmed the chamber is empty.
steps.quote: With the firearm pointed in a safe direction, remove the magazine by pressing the magazine catch (Figure 14). Let the magazine drop out of the magazine well or remove it manually.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Unloading Your Firearm, printed p.10

steps.title: Lock the slide back and LOOK — not at the indicator
steps.action: Pull the slide fully rearward by the rear serrations, ejecting anything in the chamber, and lock it open on the slide catch. Then look into the ejection port, at the chamber itself, and into the magazine well.
steps.prose: ⛔ Anderson is explicit that the loaded chamber indicator is not the check. It is an indicator; your eyes are the check.
steps.quote: Verify that the chamber is clear by looking into the ejection port and checking the chamber itself (Figure 16). Also, verify that the magazine well is empty (Figure 17).
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Unloading Your Firearm, printed p.10
steps.warn: Always visually check to be sure the chamber is empty and that no magazine is in the magazine well. Do not rely on the Loaded Chamber Indicator. Never take someone else's word that a firearm is unloaded. Check for yourself.

steps.title: Close the slide, then pull the trigger
steps.action: With the chamber and magazine well proven empty, let the slide forward and — still pointed somewhere safe — pull the trigger. The striker has to be released before the slide will come off.
steps.prose: This is the step people balk at, and it is where negligent discharges happen on this pattern of pistol. The safeguard is not skipping it — it is having already proven the chamber empty with your eyes, twice.
steps.quote: While keeping the firearm pointed in a safe direction, you may pull the trigger. With the trigger in the rearward position, the firearm is incapable of firing unless the slide is cycled again (Figure 18).
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Unloading Your Firearm, printed p.10

steps.title: ⛔ Slide back 1/8 INCH — no further
steps.action: Thumb on the back of the grip, fingers over the top of the slide, and squeeze so the slide moves back about 1/8 inch (3 mm). Hold it there.
steps.prose: ⛔ Too far and the trigger resets, and then nothing comes apart until you have pointed it safely and pulled the trigger again. 1/8 inch is a grip-squeeze, not a rack.
steps.quote: Squeeze so that the slide moves back around 1/8 inch or 3mm (Figure 20). If the slide moves back too far it will cause the trigger to reset, and you'll have to pull the trigger again (with the muzzle pointed in a safe direction).
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Disassembly, printed pp.14-15

steps.title: Slide lock DOWN on both sides, then slide forward
steps.action: Still holding the slide back that 1/8 inch, push down on BOTH sides of the slide lock with your other hand. Then run the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: Both sides. One-sided pressure cants the lock and it binds — that is the whole reason this feels stiff when it goes wrong.
steps.quote: While continuing to hold the slide back 1/8 inch or 3mm, using your other hand, push down on both sides of the slide lock (Figure 21).
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Disassembly, printed pp.14-15

steps.title: Recoil spring out, then the barrel
steps.action: Grasp the recoil spring at the rear, compress it slightly, then lift the rear and take it out of the slide. Then lift the rear of the barrel and slide it back until the muzzle clears the front of the slide, and lift it out.
steps.prose: Barrel back and up, not straight up — the muzzle has to clear its hole at the front of the slide first.
steps.quote: To remove the barrel, lift the rear of the barrel and slide it back until the muzzle clears the hole at the front of the slide, then lift it out of the slide (Figure 25&26).
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Disassembly, printed pp.14-15
steps.warn: Do not disassemble your firearm further than described. Any further disassembly will void your warranty. If you think further disassembly is necessary, contact Anderson Manufacturing.

steps.title: Barrel from the CHAMBER end, never reversing the brush
steps.action: Wet a patch with lubricant and push it through the barrel several times from the chamber end. Then a wetted brush all the way through and all the way back — never reversing while it is inside. Repeat until a fresh patch comes through clean, then one dry patch.
steps.prose: Chamber end every time, so nothing is dragged across the crown. And reversing a brush mid-bore is how bristles come off and lodge.
steps.aside: Push a new, dry, cleaning patch through the barrel from the chamber end to remove any excess lubricant.
steps.quote: Wet a cleaning brush with lubricant and push it all the way through the barrel, then pull it back all the way through. Do not reverse direction while the brush is inside the barrel. Repeat several times.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Cleaning, printed pp.16-17

steps.title: ⛔ Slide MUZZLE-DOWN while you do the breech face
steps.action: Hold the slide with the muzzle end pointing DOWN, and brush the breech face and the area around the extractor claw with an oiled nylon bristle brush. Wipe with a clean patch and repeat until it stays clean.
steps.prose: ⛔ The orientation IS the instruction. Anything liquid that reaches the firing pin hole runs down into the channel, and a striker channel with oil in it collects carbon and eventually gives you light strikes.
steps.quote: Avoid letting any lubricant, oil or other fluid get into the firing pin hole in the breech face. Keep the slide oriented with the muzzle end down while cleaning the breech face area.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Cleaning, printed pp.16-17

steps.title: Rail cuts in the slide, then the frame
steps.action: Brush the rail cuts inside the slide with an oiled nylon brush and wipe them until the cloth stays clean. Then wipe down the exposed parts of the frame with a lightly lubricated lint-free cloth.
steps.prose: The frame is a wipe-down and nothing more — Anderson says further disassembly of the frame is neither necessary nor recommended, and on a polymer frame there is nothing there an owner should be prying at.
steps.quote: Wipe down any exposed pieces of the frame as necessary with a clean, lightly lubricated, lintfree cloth. Further disassembly of the frame is not necessary or recommended.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Cleaning, printed pp.16-17

steps.title: ⛔ Five lubrication points, and one channel that stays dry
steps.action: Oil the outer surface of the barrel; inside the top of the slide where it contacts the barrel near the ejection port and near the front; a drop on EACH slide rail cut; a wipe over the outside of the slide; and a drop on the rear of the trigger bar where it meets the connector. ⛔ Nothing in the firing pin channel.
steps.prose: ⛔ Anderson adds a rule most manuals leave out: everything that is NOT a lubrication point should be DRY before the pistol goes back together. Oil that is not doing a job is collecting grit.
steps.aside: Spread a drop of oil on each of the slide rail cuts (Figure 28).
steps.quote: Do not put lubricant in the firing pin channel. Ensure all non-lubrication points are dry prior to assembly.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Lubrication, printed p.17

steps.title: Field strip complete — four pieces
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring. Anderson's published procedure ends here and going further voids the warranty by its own statement.
steps.prose: ⛔ And two things must not be done while it is apart: do not manually reset and pull the trigger, and do not let the firing pin snap forward. Both damage the very safeties you are about to test.
steps.quote: Never manually reset and pull the trigger with the firearm disassembled. This may damage the trigger safety. Do not pull the firing pin and allow it to snap forward with your firearm disassembled. This may damage the firing pin and/or firing pin safety.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Disassembly, printed pp.14-15

deepSteps.title: ⛔ This is inspection, not further stripping
deepSteps.action: With the pistol in its four field-strip pieces, work through Anderson's own inspection sequence before it goes back together. Nothing else comes apart.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Anderson's deep procedure is a set of CHECKS, and it is the honest shape of a deep clean on a pistol whose maker forbids going further. The instruction attached to a failure is unambiguous.
deepSteps.quote: If any part or parts of the firearm are found to be cracked, bent, bulged, or otherwise in worse condition than when it was when new, discontinue use immediately and contact Anderson Manufacturing for repair or replacement.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Inspection, printed pp.18-19

deepSteps.title: Barrel: lead, bulges, cracks, obstructions
deepSteps.action: Look through the bore against a light and along the outside of the barrel. You are looking for lead build-up, a bulge, a crack or anything left in the bore.
deepSteps.prose: A bulge is visible from the outside as a ring and felt as a swelling under a fingertip run down the barrel. On a 9mm it is nearly always the result of a squib that was fired over.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the barrel for lead buildup, bulges, cracks, and obstructions.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Inspection, printed pp.18-19

deepSteps.title: Frame: slide lock, catch, trigger, and the EJECTOR
deepSteps.action: Check the external surfaces of the frame including the slide lock, magazine catch, trigger and trigger safety. Check the ejector is not bent or broken. Pull up on the slide catch and confirm it springs back down.
deepSteps.prose: The ejector is the one worth a hard look on a Glock-pattern pistol — it is a small bent tab, it is what throws the case, and a bent one gives you erratic ejection and stovepipes long before it snaps.
deepSteps.quote: Check the ejector to ensure it is not bent or broken. Pull upward on the slide catch and be sure it springs back down when released.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Inspection, printed pp.18-19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The firing pin safety test — both halves
deepSteps.action: Pull the firing pin lug back and ease it forward until it stops on the firing pin safety; push forward gently and confirm the pin does NOT protrude past the breech face. Then depress the firing pin safety, hold it down, push the lug forward, and confirm the pin DOES protrude.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Two halves, and both are needed: the first proves the safety blocks, the second proves it releases. A safety that blocks but never releases is a dead pistol; one that releases but never blocks is a dangerous one. ⛔ Do not let the firing pin strike the safety freely while you do it.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin is under spring tension. Do not let the firing pin strike the firing pin safety freely, or damage may occur. If your firearm fails the firing pin safety test, discontinue use immediately and contact Anderson Manufacturing for repair.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Inspection, printed pp.18-19

deepSteps.title: Magazines: feed lips and a follower that does not hang
deepSteps.action: Look at the feed lips for bends or breaks, then press the follower down and release it. It should move freely and not hang up in the tube.
deepSteps.prose: A hanging follower is the most common cause of a failure to feed on the last two rounds, and it is usually dirt rather than a spring.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect your magazines visually to be sure the feed lips aren't bent or broken. Test that the follower moves freely by pressing down on it and releasing. It should not hang up in the magazine.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Inspection, printed pp.18-19

deepSteps.title: Reassemble, then the trigger-safety and reset tests
deepSteps.action: Barrel in, recoil spring in with the SMALLER end forward, slide onto the frame with BOTH front guide rails engaged. Then, with the chamber and magazine well verified empty: pull on the SIDES of the trigger — the trigger safety should not let it move far enough to dry fire. Then dry fire properly, hold the trigger back, cycle the slide, release the trigger and listen for the reset click. Repeat several times.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Both front guide rails before the slide goes all the way on — Anderson flags it as "Important", and a slide started on one rail is how a rail gets peened.
deepSteps.aside: Test the trigger safety only after you have verified the chamber and magazine well are empty by pulling on the sides of the trigger (Figure 39) while keeping the firearm pointed in a safe direction. The trigger safety should not allow the trigger to move far enough to dry fire the pistol.
deepSteps.quote: Be sure you have engaged both front guide rails before pushing the slide all the way onto the frame.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing Kiger Series Handguns — Operation and Safety Manual — Rev B — Assembly & Unloaded Function Testing, printed pp.20-21

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Wet patch from the CHAMBER end, several passes
Brush all the way through and back — never reverse inside
Dry patch last, then a lightly oiled wipe outside

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: ⛔ Muzzle DOWN while doing the breech face and extractor
Rail cuts brushed with an oiled nylon brush, then wiped
⛔ Nothing wet near the firing pin hole

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Wipe exposed parts with a lightly lubricated lint-free cloth
A drop of oil on the trigger bar where it meets the connector

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Follower pressed and released — it must not hang

reassembly: Barrel into the slide: muzzle through the hole first, then push the rear of the barrel into its cutout so it drops into place.
Recoil spring with the SMALLER end into the front of the slide; compress slightly and press the rear into the second notch of the barrel, closest to the muzzle.
⛔ Rack the slide onto the frame with BOTH front guide rails engaged before pushing it all the way on.
Pull the slide fully back and lock it on the slide catch; with EMPTY magazines, check the catch holds it.
Release the slide, then run the trigger-safety and reset checks before the pistol goes away.
fncheck: Chamber and magazine well verified empty by eye, muzzle safe, empty magazine only. (1) Pull on the SIDES of the trigger — the trigger safety must stop it short of firing. (2) Pull the trigger properly: it should move to the rear with an audible click. (3) Hold the trigger back, cycle the slide, release the trigger — you should hear the reset click and the trigger should snap forward. Repeat several times. (4) With an empty magazine in, pull the slide back and confirm the slide catch holds it open. Anything that fails goes back to Anderson, not to a workbench.
